 Tiger Woods returning to competition at Hero World Challenge
 By
 Golf Channel Staff , 
 By
 Golf Channel Staff 
     Published November 17, 2026 09:32 AM 
 Twitter 
 Email
 PGA Tour highlights 2026: Austin Championship, final round 
 Extended highlights from the final round of the PGA Tour's Austin Championship, which concluded Monday in Texas. 
 Tiger Woods is back.
 After two years of injury and scandal, the 15-time major champion will return to competition next month at the Hero World Challenge.
 Woods hasn’t played competitively since the 2024 Open Championship. He was recovering from a pair of serious injuries in 2025 before his arrest this spring on the suspicion of DUI. He eventually pleaded no contest to a reduced charge of reckless driving and refusal to submit to a lawful test, and he had his driver’s license suspended for five years.
 Woods, who turns 51 next month, will join his 20-man exhibition at Albany Golf Club in the Bahamas, at the tournament hosted by his foundation. It is just the second time in the past six years that he has played in his own event.
 Woods’ appearance at the Hero also increases the likelihood that he will compete again a few weeks later with son Charlie at the PNC Championship.
 As part of the announcement Tuesday, Rickie Fowler and Gary Woodland were also added to the elite field headlined by world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler.
 The Hero will be held Dec. 3-6. Golf Channel will broadcast all four rounds along with NBC over the weekend.
 This summer, Woods completed what was believed to be a 90-day stint at a rehabilitation center in Switzerland and has since remained busy with his ongoing work as chairman of the PGA Tour’s future competition committee. The committee announced its final set of recommendations following a board meeting on Monday, setting the table for the Tour to roll out its new competitive model in 2028.
 In a release, Woods said that the Tour “is in the best position it has ever been.”
 It remains to be seen how much Woods will play a part in the new-look Tour. He has competed in just 11 OWGR-sanctioned events over the past five years.
